answer.rationale: A release deployed two hours before a latency-only-on-primary write-path degradation strongly suggests the release as root cause, matching B1 where rollback cleared an error spike with no customer impact. Failover (B2) remains an option if the problem is regional infrastructure, but there is no regional saturation signal (only one region affected, no evidence of primary capacity limit), and a failover during settlement peak is riskier to writes. Routing to read replicas (B5) addresses read load, not the write path currently degraded. Adding capacity (B3) is speculative without evidence of load-driven constraint. Rolling back first is cheapest, fastest, and most directly addresses the most likely cause.
